newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court says Le Monde offended Moroccan King.
newsitem.headline: French court says Le Monde offended Moroccan King.

text.p: A Paris appeals court found the French newspaper Le Monde guilty on Thursday of offending Moroccan King Hassan in a report about alleged illicit drug trafficking in his country.

The court ordered the daily's editor Jean-Marie Colombani and journalist Eric Inciyan to each pay 500 francs ($80) fines as well as a symbolic one franc (20 cents) damages and interests to the monarch.
In July, another Paris court agreed that Hassan was insulted by the November 3, 1995 article about a confidential report by a private drugs watchdog organisation.
But the court concluded the daily and Inciyan were merely doing their job in accurately reporting the group's findings "without gratuitous attack, distortion or improper interpretation".
It is against French press law to offend a foreign head of state.
The article had cited a report commissioned by the European Union from the Geopolitical Drugs Observatory (OGD), a private group based in Paris.

It quoted the OGD report as saying up to 1,500 tonnes of hashish was exported every year from Morocco, making the kingdom the world's top source of the drugs and alleged that members of the king's close entourage and former cabinet ministers were implicated.
Rabat called the report an attempt to harm Morocco at a sensitive stage of negotiations with the European Union on an association accord.
